new_statements.relation_note: Catalog has no record for kara1489; this is the first primary evidence for the language: transcribed stress placement (Kayawan, Manay variety), lexical penult vs final. No prose rule, so it can only be catalogued as data-backed, not as an author's statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No statement; the typed list marks stress with a raised tick before the stressed syllable. Of the marked items the great majority are penultimate ('bana, 'tagoq, ma'pasoq, ti'naqi, ma'tanak, 'losong, 'pasak, ko'midya, ka'gabi..), a clear minority are final (ba'lyay, mara'ig, ka'mon, wa'lya, ma'niq, ta'nom, bira'qon, bo'lyaq, ta'gob, maba'qoq, ma'lyoq, da'lyom, bunu'qon, ka'wat, ko'sog, mata'mis, gali'san), and a handful of trisyllables carry the tick word-initially ('sipaqon, 'kilaya, 'kawalya, 'dangawa, 'alyapalya). Read as: stress is lexically contrastive, penultimate by default with lexically final-stressed words, the usual Bisayan/Mansakan pattern.
new_statements.exceptions: none stated; items 1-138 are mostly left unmarked, so the list is not exhaustive
new_statements.identity_note: Hall 1971 = Mandayan of Kayawan, Manay, Davao Oriental. Zorc folder = four 1970 EPWL lists labelled Mandayan: Caraga (Davao Oriental), Boso (Mati), Kabasagan (Boston), and 'Mandayan (Mansaka): Maragusan Valley', plus a Caragueño (San Miguel, Caraga) list, an Isamal list (Kalagan group, not Mandaya), and Proto-Mansakan innovation sheets. Skoropinski et al. 2017 = Kinamayo of Bislig City, Surigao del Sur, spoken by the 'Mandaya-Kamayo' IPs; SIL tags it kyk + mry, but the language described is Kamayo [kyk, Glottolog Kamayo], not kara1489.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog is empty for kara1489. The Caraga-list ticks agree with Hall 1971 on penultimate stress for shared items (ma'pasoq, 'tagoq, 'bana, 'apa) and differ only in notation for sang gatos ('sanggatos here vs sang'gatos in Hall). The innovation sheets are Proto-Mansakan, not Mandaya-specific.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No statement anywhere in the folder (scanned of all 82 pages has no hit for stress/accent/penult; the draft chapter pages are on subgrouping). The only Mandaya stress data are the ticks on part of the Caraga list, which put stress on the penult in most marked items (ma'tobag, 'saging, ko'moqon, 'tagoq, ma'pasoq, 'pila, 'gotom, 'bana, 'apa, 'toqod) and word-initially in two trisyllables ('sanggatos, 'patayan); the Boso, Kabasagan and Maragusan lists are unmarked; the Caragueño (San Miguel) list's superscript marks are glottal-stop and ng corrections, not stress. Zorc's Mansakan-innovation sheets carry acute accents on either the final (damán, pesáq, ʔabá) or the penult (ʔísəʔ, hákuʔ) of proto-forms, i.e. lexical accent at the Proto-Mansakan level.
new_statements.identity_note: Hall 1971 = Mandayan of Kayawan, Manay, Davao Oriental. Zorc folder = four 1970 EPWL lists labelled Mandayan: Caraga (Davao Oriental), Boso (Mati), Kabasagan (Boston), and 'Mandayan (Mansaka): Maragusan Valley', plus a Caragueño (San Miguel, Caraga) list, an Isamal list (Kalagan group, not Mandaya), and Proto-Mansakan innovation sheets. Skoropinski et al. 2017 = Kinamayo of Bislig City, Surigao del Sur, spoken by the 'Mandaya-Kamayo' IPs; SIL tags it kyk + mry, but the language described is Kamayo [kyk, Glottolog Kamayo], not kara1489.

readall_conflicts: No source contradicts another; none of the three states a rule in prose. Both SIL-style wordlists (Hall 1971 Kayawan and the Caraga list in the Zorc folder) transcribe stress with a pre-syllable tick and agree on penultimate stress for shared items; they differ only in notation on one item ('sanggatos in the Caraga list vs sang'gatos in Hall) and in that a few trisyllables in each list carry the tick word-initially ('sipaqon, 'kilaya, 'kawalya in Hall; 'sanggatos, 'patayan in Caraga), which may be antepenultimate stress or a typist's convention. Hall's list also shows a minority of final-stressed words (ba'lyay, mara'ig, ka'mon, ta'nom, ko'sog, mata'mis..), so the data support lexical penult-vs-final stress rather than fixed penult. The Skoropinski 2017 guide describes Kinamayo (Kamayo, kyk) of Bislig City, not the Davao Oriental Mandaya, and its orthographic rule (grave accent marks where stress and length fall) is compatible but not evidence for kara1489.

sources.note: Phoneme inventory (17 C, 6 V incl. schwa) for Cateel, Caraga, Manay, Tarragona Mandaya. Never uses the word stress; Table 5 (p. 384) presents 'vowel lengthening' of /a:/ /u:/ (/i:/, /ə:/) as 'another distinct characteristic of Mandaya phonology', with length on the penult in /bu:yak/ 'flower', /katu:mbal/ 'chili', /sə:psəp/, but on the antepenult in /i:yayas/ 'wild pig', /magai:kol/ 'laugh'; no rule for its placement is given and it is not related to stress.
